decisions: The map's single receipt-module cut is a back-edge: _entry_receipt is annotated with ValueSource and receipt_for constructs one, and ValueSource cannot follow them out because its ref() builds a ValueRef and its receipt() calls receipt_for, so it sits above both layers. _entry_receipt and receipt_for therefore stay in value_ref.py beside ValueSource, and only the receipt record and the registry read move.

SourceReceipt validates through ValueRefError, which is the whole file's refusal, so a receipt module holding it alone would be a back-edge too. The closed vocabularies a reference is spelled in become their own leaf, reference_vocabulary.py, which value_source_receipt.py and the residue both read. That is also what lands the residue at 456 lines: the receipt record on its own is 46.
_registry moves with SourceReceipt rather than becoming public as registry_mapping. It is read at exactly one site and the two are the only readers of the registry modules for citation purposes.

Published spelling: the receipt module is value_source_receipt.py, because state_timeline.SourceReceipt is a different class of the same name and a module named for the bare concept sends a grep to the wrong home. Its registry read is live_registry, which value_ref calls across the boundary.
